newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Low inflation attracts drug gangs to Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Low inflation attracts drug gangs to Brazil.

text.p: The United States has warned Brazil that lower inflation has made Latin America's largest country an increasingly attractive place for money laundering by drug cartels, a newspaper reported on Saturday.
The Folha de Sao Paulo daily said Washington had told the Brazilian Internal Revenue Service that Brazil was 10th among countries attracting "investments" by narcotics smugglers.
Folha added that 17 percent of the Latin American drug cartels' bank accounts were thought to be in Brazil and about $450 billion in dirty money was passing through the country every year.
No one was immediately available at the U.S. embassy to comment.
Folha said drug money was being "washed" through the purchase of objects of art, thoroughbred race horses and expensive imported cars.
The Brazilian government's "Plano Real" economic stabilisation plan has brought inflation down from a peak of about 5,000 percent annually two years ago to about 20 percent a year now.
